title: Mosaic Retail Accelerator POC playbook
content:
Purpose and context:
This playbook is an operational kickoff and success-criteria checklist for the Mosaic Retail Accelerator POC. Mosaic is evaluating Redwood Inference to power store-assistant features (product search, shelf replenishment suggestions, and short-form personalized offers) across three pilot stores. The goal of the POC is to validate latency and cost targets, integration simplicity with Mosaic's point-of-sale and inventory APIs, and delivery quality on the retail prompt sets provided in the dataset pack.

Problem statement (why this POC):
- Mosaic needs a reliable inference stack that meets 95th percentile latency < 120ms for short-chat interactions and median token cost that is < $0.0008 per token for their typical query distribution.
- Existing hosted model tests show good quality but inconsistent tail latency during peak footfall windows. Mosaic requires predictable degradations and clear fallback behaviors.

Objectives (3 key outcomes):
1) Performance: Demonstrate stable P95 latency < 120ms for conversational product lookups under a load profile of 40 concurrent sessions per store.
2) Cost & Ops: Show a projected monthly inference spend that fits within Mosaic's budget envelope (estimate + buffer) and validate autoscaling behavior under traffic spikes.
3) Quality & UX: Achieve >85% accept rate from Mosaic merchant reviewers on response relevance and a <4% hallucination rate on SKU-related information during evaluation sets.

Success metrics (measurable acceptance criteria):
- Latency: P50 < 40ms, P95 < 120ms, P99 < 350ms over a three-day steady-state run mirroring peak times.
- Throughput: Sustain 120 concurrent requests across the three stores with <1% request error rate.
- Cost: Realized per-token cost within 10% of forecasted cost for configured batching/quantization profile.
- Quality: Manual eval pass >85% (relevance), hallucination rate <4%, and zero critical correctness errors on price/availability claims.
- Integration: End-to-end data flow from Mosaic inventory API to Redwood inference (including auth and transformations) completed and exercised in sandbox.
- Security & compliance: All required security controls (TLS, KMS integration for secrets, audit logging) validated by Mosaic SecOps in sandbox.

Scope and out-of-scope:
- In-scope: product-search chat flows, shelf-add suggestions, and personalized short offers. Includes connector for Mosaic Inventory API v2, sample UI wireframe integration, metrics dashboard for latency/cost.
- Out-of-scope: full POS integration for checkout authorization, loyalty program rewrites, and offline edge deployments. These can be evaluated in a later tranche if POC passes.

Team and roles:
- SE lead: Riley Chen (project owner) - overall delivery, customer syncs, acceptance sign-off.
- Solutions Eng: Aisha Navarro - connector implementation and load testing scripts.
- ML Eng: Priya Singh - model selection, quantization profiles, and quality eval harness.
- Customer Success: Diego Morales - onboarding, customer-facing runbooks, training.
- Mosaic counterparts: Ben Howard (CTO sponsor), Lina Vargas (Retail Ops), Anil Mehta (SecOps).

Timeline (6-week sprint):
Week 0 (pre-kickoff): legal/NDAs, access requests, mosaic data pack received.
Week 1: Kickoff workshop, architecture review, and alignment on dataset slices + evaluation rubric.
Week 2: Connector build and sandbox auth + initial smoke tests.
Week 3: Model selection, baseline runs, and latency profiling.
Week 4: Optimization pass (batching, KV cache tuning, quantization test) and run full-day soak test.
Week 5: Customer evaluation sessions, manual reviews, and security validation.
Week 6: Final acceptance run, retrospective, and handoff recommendations.

Kickoff workshop agenda (90 minutes):
- 0-10m: Introductions, success criteria, and key contacts.
- 10-25m: Mosaic product walkthrough and sample flows.
- 25-45m: Proposed architecture (Redwood hosted + dedicated fallback) and dataflow.
- 45-65m: Evaluation rubric deep-dive (latency, quality, cost).
- 65-80m: Integration plan and prerequisites (tokens, endpoints, test accounts).
- 80-90m: Risks, open questions, and next steps + immediate action items.

Integration checklist (sandbox):
- Service account created and scoped to sandbox inventory read-only endpoints.
- Inventory API keys & sample payloads shared (anonymized) — verify sample SKU format.
- Mapping doc: SKU -> canonical_id mapping agreed.
- Staging UI stub with sample calls for manual review.
- Audit logs enabled for all inference calls in sandbox.

Observability & evaluation tooling:
- Dashboards: latency histogram (p50/p95/p99), tokens per request, model variant breakdown, error rate, tail-kv-cache-miss ratio.
- Traces: example trace spans for end-to-end call (UI -> Redwood gateway -> model shard -> response).
- Alerting: P95 latency > 200ms sustained for 5 minutes, error rate >1% over 10 minutes.
- Eval harness: Batch job that runs curated prompt set nightly and outputs pass/fail and hallucination counts.

Security & data handling notes:
- No PII is to be sent in POC. Any customer-provided logs are scrubbed via the provided redaction script.
- Keys stored in customer KMS; Redwood uses temporary tokens scoped to sandbox.
- Audit and retention: Mosaic requested 90-day logs; retention policy configured accordingly in sandbox.

Fallback and graceful degradation strategy:
- Primary model: tuned open model X-1 (quantized).
- Fallback: smaller low-latency variant X-1-lite when queueing > 100ms per-req or if memory pressure crosses threshold.
- Read-only mode: when external inventory is unreachable, responses fall back to cached SKU suggestions with UI indicator and degrade to non-actionable suggestions.

Cost estimation approach (working):
- Attach sample workload (tokens per interaction distribution) to estimator. We'll run the estimator with three profiles: baseline (no quant), optimized (int8 quant + batching), and conservative (lite model). Mosaic finance will pick target profile.

Acceptance run recipe (how we demonstrate success):
1) Prepare 48-hour steady-state workload replay from sample-store traces with synthetic peak windows.
2) Run the workload through the chosen production-like stack (same autoscale rules).
3) Capture metrics, collect 200 manual-eval items, and compute pass rates and hallucination counts.
4) Security team runs penetration-lite checklist and confirms audit logs.
5) Mosaic stakeholders review pass/fail matrix; if all success metrics pass, Mosaic writes acceptance sign-off ticket.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: SKU hallucination in generative responses. Mitigation: Response templating + strict canonical_id lookup with fallback to "I don't know" when untrusted.
- Risk: Unexpected tail latency spikes during in-store peak scans. Mitigation: Enable autoscale margins and warm-up periods; pre-warm KV caches before peak windows.
- Risk: Data mapping mismatches. Mitigation: Early store-by-store mapping workshops and sample payload validation.

Open questions for Mosaic to resolve in week 0:
- Can Mosaic provide anonymized peak traffic traces for two representative stores?
- Which fields from the inventory API are considered "source of truth" for price and availability?
- Is there an internal sales-ops reviewer who will provide the final manual quality signoff?

Appendix: quick runbook for a live demo (5–7 minutes):
- Demo script: 1) show UI product search -> query. 2) show inference latency & tokens via live dashboard. 3) trigger a simulated high-load event and show fallback to lite model. 4) show audit log entries for the query.
- Quick troubleshooting steps: restart connector pod -> re-run sample request; if latency still high, switch to lite model via routing policy and capture traces.

Notes and next actions (immediate):
- Riley: schedule kickoff workshop with Mosaic for Jan 21; include SecOps and Mosaic product ops.
- Aisha: begin connector scaffold and share initial README by Jan 18.
- Priya: prepare three model profiles and expected token cost table by Jan 20.
- Diego: prepare onboarding runbook and evaluation rubric doc for customer reviewers by Jan 19.

This doc will be updated iteratively; version history kept in the linked Confluence page.
